definition_l2: A problem that is difficult to solve because every available option has a serious drawback.
example_sentence: Whether to hedge the currency exposure or simply absorb it is a conundrum the treasury team faces every quarter.

definition_l2: Found everywhere; so common that you stop noticing it.
example_sentence: Transformer architectures have become ubiquitous across every branch of machine learning.

definition_l2: Extremely careful about small details, to the point of checking everything.
example_sentence: Authenticating a vintage watch demands meticulous inspection of the movement and the serial numbers.

definition_l2: Holding two opposing feelings about something at the same time, so unable to decide.
example_sentence: He felt ambivalent about extending the exchange semester by another term.

definition_l2: A framework of assumptions that shapes how a whole field thinks about its subject.
example_sentence: Self-supervised pre-training marked a genuine paradigm shift in how models are trained.

definition_l2: The ability to recover quickly after damage or difficulty.
example_sentence: The portfolio showed surprising resilience through the March selloff.

translation_fr: Juxtaposer / Mettre côte à côte pour comparer
definition_l2: To place two things side by side so the contrast between them becomes visible.
example_sentence: The dashboard juxtaposes forecast revenue against actual bookings on a single axis.

definition_l2: Lasting a very short time; gone almost as soon as it appears.
example_sentence: Attention on a new AI product is ephemeral; most launches are forgotten within a fortnight.

definition_l2: Appearing entirely harmless — often used when something turned out not to be.
example_sentence: An innocuous-looking config change brought down the entire deployment.

definition_l2: Judging by what actually works rather than by theory or principle.
example_sentence: We took a pragmatic approach and shipped the smallest version that actually worked.

definition_l2: Wanting to punish someone who has wronged you, often quietly and over time.
example_sentence: A vindictive supplier can quietly deprioritise your orders for months without ever saying so.

definition_l2: So complicated and twisted that it becomes hard to follow.
example_sentence: The pricing logic had grown so convoluted that nobody in the team could explain it.

definition_l2: Stated as the reason, while the real reason is something else.
example_sentence: The ostensible reason for the merger was scale; the real driver was access to the Asian market.

definition_l2: A small distinction that changes the meaning, easily missed.
example_sentence: A DCF hides a great deal of nuance inside the terminal growth assumption.

definition_l2: To perceive something that is not obvious, especially by looking carefully.
example_sentence: It is difficult to discern a genuine signal from noise in a sample this small.

definition_l2: Honest and direct, especially when the truth is uncomfortable.
example_sentence: Her candid feedback on my application was far more useful than polished praise.

definition_l2: Chosen without a reason that can be defended; it could just as well have been otherwise.
example_sentence: Choosing five clusters felt arbitrary until we ran the silhouette analysis.

definition_l2: Holding together logically, so each part follows from the last.
example_sentence: The pitch needs a coherent narrative, not merely a sequence of impressive charts.

definition_l2: To draw out a response or reaction that would not have come on its own.
example_sentence: The survey was designed to elicit honest answers about what customers would actually pay.

definition_l2: To make an already bad situation worse.
example_sentence: Port congestion in Singapore exacerbated delays right across the supply chain.

definition_l2: Possible to do with the time, money and people actually available.
example_sentence: Is it feasible to deploy the whole pipeline before the semester ends?

definition_l2: To slow something down or make it harder, without stopping it entirely.
example_sentence: Poor documentation hinders every new developer who joins the project.

definition_l2: Certain to happen; impossible to prevent.
example_sentence: Some drift in model performance is inevitable once the data distribution shifts.

definition_l2: Made of many small parts fitted together with great precision.
example_sentence: The perpetual calendar is the most intricate complication on the workshop bench.

definition_l2: Expressed so clearly that a difficult idea becomes easy to follow.
example_sentence: His explanation of gradient descent was the most lucid account I had read.

definition_l2: Far smaller than what is needed.
example_sentence: The startup ran on a meager budget for its first two years.

definition_l2: An idea or belief, often loosely held rather than carefully worked out.
example_sentence: The notion that markets are perfectly efficient is hard to defend empirically.

definition_l2: No longer used, because something better has replaced it.
example_sentence: Quartz movements rendered a whole generation of mechanical calibres commercially obsolete.

definition_l2: On the edge of what matters; not central to the main question.
example_sentence: Offline sync is essential; the stats dashboard is peripheral for now.

definition_l2: Believable on the surface, though not necessarily true.
example_sentence: The forecast is plausible, but it rests on one very optimistic assumption.

definition_l2: Unstable, and likely to collapse if one thing goes wrong.
example_sentence: A boutique that depends on three suppliers is in a precarious position.

definition_l2: Widespread within a particular group or place.
example_sentence: Missing values were far more prevalent in the older records than in recent ones.

definition_l2: Given by each side to the other; going both ways.
example_sentence: Good professional relationships are reciprocal rather than transactional.

definition_l2: Not needed, because the same thing is already provided elsewhere.
example_sentence: The reviewer flagged three redundant checks that the type system already guaranteed.

definition_l2: Sharply and plainly obvious, with nothing softening it.
example_sentence: There was a stark contrast between retail margins in Singapore and in Europe.

definition_l2: So slight that it takes attention to notice, yet it changes things.
example_sentence: There is a subtle difference between correlation in the sample and in the population.

definition_l2: Real and concrete enough to be measured or pointed at.
example_sentence: Recruiters want tangible results, not a list of technologies you have touched once.

definition_l2: Provisional and not yet confirmed; may still change.
example_sentence: We reached a tentative agreement on the internship dates, pending visa confirmation.

definition_l2: Complete in every detail, leaving nothing unchecked.
example_sentence: The reviewer ran a thorough pass over the database migration before we deployed it.

definition_l2: Of so little importance that it does not deserve attention.
example_sentence: The bug looked trivial and cost us an entire afternoon.

definition_l2: Never having happened before, so there is nothing to compare it to.
example_sentence: Container shipping rates reached unprecedented levels that year.

definition_l2: Able to work and keep working under real conditions.
example_sentence: A subscription-free flashcard app is only viable if the hosting costs nothing.

definition_l2: Changing suddenly and unpredictably, often sharply.
example_sentence: Freight rates are notoriously volatile, which makes forecasting margins difficult.

definition_l2: Cautious because you suspect a risk that is not yet proven.
example_sentence: Be wary of any backtest that has never seen out-of-sample data.

definition_l2: Highly skilled at something, especially something difficult.
example_sentence: She is adept at turning a messy dataset into something a board can actually read.

definition_l2: Distant and uninvolved, whether by choice or by appearance.
example_sentence: He came across as aloof at the networking evening, though he was simply exhausted.

definition_l2: Open to more than one interpretation, so the intended meaning is unclear.
example_sentence: An ambiguous specification is precisely how two agents produce incompatible implementations.

definition_l2: Requiring sustained hard effort over a long period.
example_sentence: The visa process for the internship turned out to be long and arduous.

definition_l2: So ordinary and predictable that it is dull.
example_sentence: Most build-in-public posts are banal; the interesting ones show the failures.

definition_l2: The quality of using few words.
example_sentence: In a cover letter, brevity signals confidence more reliably than length ever does.
